18870174_6fe8e880.text: In area CA1, Sánchez-Aguilera et al. (2014) identified a deep subpopulation of pyramidal cells that expresses a broad range of markers, among them Ctip2, Sox5, muscarinic acetylcholine receptor M1, and several neuropeptides, including somatostatin and neuropeptide Y. In rats and mice, these cells were shown to have a large body and a local axon plexus in stratum oriens and were termed "trilaminar cells". In the monkey, they may correspond to "profusely branching or radiatum cells" (Buckmaster and Amaral 2001). Over 50 % of the trilaminar cells project to subcortical targets, including the septum, olfactory bulb, and hypothalamus (Sik et al. 1994, 1995), and they innervate local interneurons (Gulyás et al. 1998). They are thought to coordinate the septohippocampal networks during sleep-related oscillations (Sik et al. 1994).
